$comment_shimPackages: Packages that work on Windows only, whose API a shim gives on .NET (experiments/wf4c/shims, referenced by every converted project): removed from the projects, id -> why.

$comment_droppedPackages: In the box on .NET, or tooling of the .NET Framework build. System.* 4.x packages are dropped as well.
$comment_frameworkReferences: .NET Framework assembly references (no HintPath) with a .NET 10 answer. Others are in the box or have none.
$comment_frameworkCompanions: Added along with a framework reference: what the .NET Framework assembly also contained.
$comment_noAnswer: Assemblies .NET has no counterpart for (reported; the code using them is stubbed; left out of web.config's page compilation, where loading them fails every page). Designers' (System.Design, System.Web.Extensions.Design: Visual Studio's) the desktop's (System.Windows.Forms: Windows desktop applications', not a web application's), and ASP.NET's chart controls (System.Web.DataVisualization).
$comment_sourcePackages: What .NET Framework had in its own assemblies and .NET ships as packages: added when the sources use it.

$comment_namespaceMoves: Namespaces and types a package moved: where the build does not find them (CS0234, CS0246), the sources name them where they are now. Entity Framework 4, .NET Framework's own (System.Data.Entity), is EF6 on .NET (Upgrading to EF6: its core types in System.Data.Entity.Core).
$comment_namespaceMovesOption: The choice the moves are of: Entity Framework 4 to EF6.
$comment_frameworkAssets: Packages whose .NET asset has another API than the .NET Framework one the site ran: that one is referenced (restored, not compiled against). The DLL in the package, and why.

$comment_platformReplacements: Members that work on Windows only (they compile, and throw PlatformNotSupportedException elsewhere) or otherwise elsewhere, replaced by FrameworkOnCore.Compat's, which is the same on Windows. By symbol (FrameworkOnCore.Analyzers' PlatformAnalyzer, FOC1006; C# and Visual Basic): member is the type's full name and the member's (.ctor: a constructor); then: a property read on its value, the read replaced; arguments: the call's count; parameterType: a type one of its parameters has. replace: expression (the whole expression becomes the replacement) or call (the call keeps its arguments; a call on an object passes it first). The first rule that applies.
